Prior work treats knowledge as static, missing how multimodal information is fused over time. DyMRL merges time-specific features from Euclidean, hyperbolic, and complex spaces inside a message-passing framework. This captures deep geometric features. For fusion, it tracks how each modality's past contributions shift over time. The aim is sharper forecasts from evolving knowledge.
arxiv-2603-25036: Das and co-authors track the X-ray behavior of neutron star binary 4U 1820-30 across six years of AstroSat data. The source sat in its banana state through the visits. The team split its color track into eleven segments and fit each spectrum. A warm disk plus Compton-scattered light from a hot boundary layer fits well. The disk edge sits 19 to 40 kilometers out, and the hot layer makes about 80 percent of the flux. Timing checks find fast flickers near 710 and 740 hertz, stronger at high energies.
arxiv-2603-25436: Lastrucci and co-authors sharpen neutrino signals in real time on the JUNO detector's own electronics. JUNO's light sensors produce floods of data, and faint events drown in background noise. Their Wiener deconvolution runs on FPGA boards inside the readout chain. It rebuilds each sensor pulse as it arrives, with tiny delay and high throughput. Cleaner low-energy events can then be kept instead of dropped for storage reasons. That matters for brief cosmic flashes. Board tests show the design holds up at full stream rates.
arxiv-2603-25636: Yang describes a system that designs imaging instruments from a one-sentence request. Choosing operators and settings for an imaging system can take weeks of expert work. The approach uses a structured format called spec.md and three agents named Plan, Judge, and Execute. Together they turn plain language into a validated forward model. A theorem splits the total reconstruction error into five bounded parts, each tied to a fix. On six real-data modalities, the authors report quality matching expert libraries.
arxiv-2603-25936: Moreno and Durran ask whether climate models need their usual cloud parameterizations to get rainfall right. Standard models struggle with deep convection and cloud microphysics schemes. The authors bypass both with a machine learning model. It reads 13 ERA5 fields that are easy to observe and predicts surface precipitation. One version trains on ERA5 rain, another on satellite data. The satellite-trained model matches the daily rain cycle and extremes well. It also cuts the excess light rain seen in ERA5.
arxiv-2603-26036: Uddin, Tasnim, and Oh present Face2Parts, a deepfake detector that reads faces from coarse to fine. Past detectors each focus on one region, like lips or eyes. Face2Parts extracts features from the full frame, the face, and key parts separately. It then models how those regions relate to each other. A channel-attention step and triplet learning capture the links. On the FF++ benchmark, the method scores an AUC of 98.42 percent. Scores stay strong across eight datasets and many manipulation types, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-26236: Kialy, Shtarkberg, and Klein ask whether language models treat slang as one shared idea or as facts tied to each tongue. They probe the Gemma-2-9B-IT model with sparse autoencoders in English, Hebrew, and Russian. Each test word can be read in a plain sense or a slang sense. They find a small shared core of features for informal tone, strongest in deep layers. Steering those features shifts formality in all three tongues, and in six more unseen ones.
arxiv-2603-26336: Aslam and co-authors propose a way to hide private traits in video while keeping action recognition working. Video models can pick up face identity and other traits, and motion itself can act as a biometric cue. Their method splits action traits from privacy traits inside a vision transformer, using two special tokens. A score then ranks each space-time tubelet, and only the top ones are kept. Tests show the pruning cuts privacy cues while holding on to action cues.
arxiv-2603-26636: Sasatani and Kawahara design a room-scale wireless power system with no obstacles inside the charging space. Multimode cavity resonance can fill a whole volume, but past designs needed a central pole. Their patched-wall resonator links conductive wall segments with capacitors instead. Two resonant modes together cover both the room's edges and its centre. Simulations over a 54 cubic metre enclosure show at least 48.1% transfer efficiency everywhere inside. The open volume keeps the space usable while devices charge.
arxiv-2603-26836: Bairagi and co-authors aim to measure heart rate from face video without any contact sensor. Such signals break down under motion, shadows, and changing light. Their weighted map rates each pixel's reliability and suppresses noisy regions. A contrastive learning setup then trains a Swin-Unet on these maps. A wavelet map that keeps motion but removes pulse cues serves as the negative example. On public benchmarks, the method cut heart rate error below prior self-supervised approaches.
arxiv-2603-27236: Parra and co-authors open a three-part XRISM study by untangling the crowded Galactic center field itself. The target transient sits just 18 arcseconds from the supermassive black hole Sgr A*. Supernova remnant emission and diffuse Galactic center glow contaminate the same field. A nearby neutron star binary was also in outburst during the March 2025 observation. The team models background and spatial-spectral mixing with two approaches. The cleaned framework supports the spectral studies that follow in the series. XMM-Newton and NuSTAR coverage anchors the joint analysis.
arxiv-2603-27436: Polo and Prodan pin down all heat states of abelian Kitaev models. Such models place spins on a lattice with vertex and face rules. The authors first show a key subalgebra acts as a diagonal part. That step lets them view the whole system as a groupoid algebra. Heat flow then comes from a groupoid cocycle. For each inverse temperature, exactly one KMS state exists. As temperature drops to zero, that state meets the ground state.
arxiv-2603-27636: Robens surveys what extra scalar particles could mean for particle physics. Extended scalar sectors add new Higgs-like states. Light scalars draw focus at future Higgs factories. Much of the talk centers on the Inert Doublet model. That model hides a dark scalar doublet. Recent studies probe its reach at lepton colliders. The survey picks out key search channels. It serves as a compact field update.
arxiv-2603-27736: Fischer proves three hardness guesses for shortest paths are one and the same. The APSP hypothesis says all-pairs paths need near-cubic time. Stronger forms cover small weights and unweighted graphs. A universe reduction links all three claims. The proof assumes fast matrix products and a combinatorics premise. Many side problems gain matching lower bounds. Node-weighted paths and bottleneck paths are among them.
arxiv-2603-28136: Thomsen and six co-authors measure how magnetic layers talk to each other in a van der Waals stack. They image an Fe3GeTe2 and graphite sandwich with Lorentz microscopy and electron holography, in cross-section. The maps rebuild the local magnetic field inside and between the layers. Domain alignment fades as the layers separate, giving a coupling length near 37 nanometers. Surface effects also weaken the field up to about 100 nanometers deep, a guide for device design.
arxiv-2603-28236: Xing classifies higher cluster tilting subcategories inside d-Nakayama algebras. These algebras come with one built-in dZ-cluster tilting subcategory. Xing asks which of them admit an ndZ version for n above 1. The radical square zero case was settled by earlier work. For each other non-self-injective algebra, he lists all such subcategories, and there is at most one. For self-injective cases, he gives number conditions on the algebra's two parameters and builds an example.
arxiv-2603-28336: Serrano, Kevari, and Narayan present a multi-agent pipeline that reviews research literature in a non-linear, rhizome-like way. Standard reviews filter by keywords in a tree shape and miss sideways links between fields. Their system runs 12 agents through seven phases, pulling papers from OpenAlex and arXiv. It maps topics with SciBERT and watches for ruptures in the network. Early runs surfaced cross-field links and gaps that normal screening overlooks. The code is open source.
arxiv-2603-28436: Hidalgo and five co-authors build a hearing aid speech cleaner as one Bayesian generative model. Fixed, hand-tuned settings fail when rooms and listeners change. Their framework treats processing, learning, and personal taste as inference in a single state-space model, with uncertainty tracked throughout. It grows out of spectral subtraction and adapts itself to each user and setting. On the VoiceBank+DEMAND corpus it matched strong rivals with only 85 effective parameters, running in real time.
arxiv-2603-28736: Montaner and co-authors present a way to tune radio digital twins for joint sensing and communication. The method joins fine ray tracing with wideband channel sounding. That pairing keeps sim and lab results aligned. They test the approach in urban settings with mono-static and bi-static setups. Moving user platforms and vehicles take part. The tuned twin matched multipath shifts, moving scatterers, and Doppler traits well. Exact geometry, materials, antenna patterns, and diffuse scattering proved key. It offers a scalable tool for testing 6G sensing and communication algorithms.
arxiv-2603-29036: Ham and co-authors generate humanless walkthroughs of environments from egocentric walking tour videos. Such videos hold image data, but crowds fill many frames. Their algorithm removes humans and their shadow effects by inpainting. A semi-synthetic dataset of video clip pairs trains the model. Each pair joins a clean background clip with a composite clip of humans and simulated shadows. Both parts came from real tour videos. A fine-tuned Casper video diffusion model beat the base model by clear margins.
arxiv-2603-29236: Udugama and co-authors present M2H-MX, a real-time perception model for single-camera robots. One camera is cheap and easy to mount, but spatial understanding from it stays hard. Their model predicts depth and scene labels together in one decoder. Gated context and cross-task links let the two outputs reinforce each other. The outputs feed a standard monocular SLAM pipeline unchanged. On NYUDv2, their large model raised label scores by 6.6 percent over strong baselines. Depth error fell by 9.4 percent on the same test set.
arxiv-2603-29836: Fischer and Gangl prove two new Littlewood identities for spin Hall-Littlewood functions. These fully inhomogeneous rational functions arise as partition functions in higher spin vertex models. One identity writes a weighted sum over partitions as two simple products. The other brings in a Pfaffian factor. A corollary gives a fresh identity for classic Hall-Littlewood polynomials. A link to modified Robbins polynomials helped them find the results. They also build a bijection between the underlying models.
arxiv-2603-30036: Kaufmann and co-authors ask when training a model's chain-of-thought hurts our ability to monitor it. Monitors read the reasoning trace to oversee AI systems. Training can teach models to hide key reasoning features. Their frame splits reward into an output term and a trace term. Each pair is classed as aligned, orthogonal, or in-conflict before training. Tests confirm in-conflict rewards cut monitorability. Such rewards also prove hard to optimize.
arxiv-2604-00436: Tang and colleagues study how developers actually program with AI assistants inside code editors. Past studies used small lab setups or general chatbots, missing workflows where the assistant sees the codebase and edits many files. Drawing on chats committed to public repositories during normal work, the team covers 74,998 developer messages and 11,579 sessions, spanning 899 developers and 1,300 repositories, using Cursor and GitHub Copilot. Their findings trace three shifts in programming habits with AI help.
arxiv-2604-00536: Fan and colleagues propose OptimSyn, a way to optimise rubrics for synthetic training data using influence signals. Supervised fine-tuning data in medicine, law, and finance is scarce. Expert curation costs much, privacy binds tightly, and labels prove hard to keep consistent. Practice prompts a generator over domain documents and filters outputs with handcrafted rubrics. But rubric design stays expert-dependent, transfers poorly, and gets tuned through a brittle loop of guesswork. OptimSyn aims to supply the missing quantitative feedback, guiding rubric choice by influence on downstream performance.
arxiv-2604-00936: Askholm, Johnsen, and Mauro report an industry migration of a Jenkins-based COBOL pipeline at Bankdata, a co-op IT firm for Danish banks. The old design spread Groovy scripts across four repositories with runtime dependency installation, making it fragile, slow, and locked to platform-specific logic. Moving to containers with an abstraction layer, a simpler repository structure, and a pre-built OCI-compliant image cut runtime by 82 percent. It yields lessons on abstraction, use of containers, and team adoption.
arxiv-2604-01036: Schirmer and team study popularity bias in recommender systems through user-recommender alignment, where picks favor popular items over users' tastes for popular or niche content. They introduce Popularity Quantile Calibration, gauging the gap between a user's past popularity taste and their picks' popularity. Building on it, they propose SPREE, a run-time fix for ordered pickers using signal steering: it finds a popularity angle in feature space and steers signals per user, varying angle and strength. Across datasets, SPREE always lifts user popularity alignment while keeping pick quality.
arxiv-2604-01836: Heidarianbaei and colleagues present a texture transformer for segmenting textured non-manifold 3D meshes, whose irregular structure challenges learning. Recent mesh methods ignore rich textural information. Their model learns from raw pixels per mesh face, with layered multi-scale aggregation. A texture branch turns face-level pixels into a learned token, fused with shape descriptors and processed by Two-Stage Blocks for local and global flow. On the Semantic Urban Meshes benchmark and a new roof-tile dataset annotated for damage, the method reaches 81.9 percent mF1, beating existing approaches.
arxiv-2604-01936: Faye and colleagues sharpen propaganda detection in news with a neurosymbolic mix of text embeddings and symbolic clues. Propaganda pieces blend slanted messages with factual reports, and pure language models tend to memorize their training sources rather than cope with new ones. The team pairs fastText embeddings with genre, topic and persuasion features, lifting accuracy over text-only rivals. Ablation and explanation checks confirm the added features drive the gain, pointing to a sturdier classifier for new outlets.
arxiv-2604-02836: Kim and four colleagues introduce Fact-Hash, a parameter-encoding method for training neural radiance fields directly on edge devices. On-device training promises privacy and fast adaptation to changing scenes, but GPU memory, storage, and power limits block deployment. Fact-Hash merges tensor factorization with hash encoding, projecting 3D coordinates into lower-dimensional forms before hashing. It cuts memory use by over one-third while preserving rendering quality and speed.
arxiv-2604-02936: Pasic and four colleagues analyze pilot-aided channel estimation for millimeter-wave MIMO systems using out-of-band sub-6 GHz information, in static and dynamic scenarios. Future systems pair fully digital beamforming MIMO at millimeter-wave frequencies with conventional sub-6 GHz systems, creating chances to borrow lower-band information for channel estimation. Simulations show incorporating sub-6 GHz information yields notable spectral efficiency gains for line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight conditions alike.
arxiv-2604-03036: Ghosh and Ramachandran settle Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian's question on the minimal area of polynomial lemniscates. They constrain every zero of the polynomial to lie on a compact set whose logarithmic capacity exceeds 1. They show the minimal area shrinks exponentially fast, and prove Fekete polynomials minimize the area in the limit.
arxiv-2604-03136: Russell and colleagues test whether machine-written fiction can be told from human fiction by story structure alone, ignoring surface style. Their StoryScope pipeline extracts 304 narrative features per story across 61,608 stories, and structure alone nearly matches style-based detection. Machine stories cluster together with tidy plots and over-explained themes, while human stories spread wider with murkier choices and tangled timelines.
arxiv-2604-03236: Jayaweera, Huang, and Dorr test BLADE, a course-grounded tutoring assistant that guides students to materials through cited dialogue instead of handing over answers. In an advanced undergraduate NLP course, students given BLADE alone scored highest on quizzes, and students offered both BLADE and direct materials chose BLADE yet scored lower. The team warns that adding direct access can add mental load without benefit.
arxiv-2604-03336: Savdhariya fills a gap for ternary-weight language models, which had no native binary wire format. His NativeTernary scheme encodes weights at exactly 2 bits each on the BitNet b1.58 architecture, shrinking headers 460-fold against GGUF while keeping encode and decode speeds practical on ordinary hardware. Its decoder is a tiny ten-line stateless machine that tolerates bitstream corruption.
arxiv-2604-03436: Levinson tackles a flaw in sparse autoencoders: units meant to stand for single concepts often blend several hidden subspaces. His joint training adds a penalty for such blending, using a small meta autoencoder that rebuilds the main model's decoder directions. The chosen setup cuts mean size about 8 percent and lifts fuzzing scores about 8 percent on GPT-2 large.
arxiv-2604-03536: Ong and colleagues propose SafeSpace, a way to unite many small certified safe sets into one big certified safe set for control systems. A helper value lets individual barrier functions combine with AND/OR logic, yielding a broad combined barrier function when a match rule holds. The resulting safety filter runs without breaks over the combined region. It is shown on two spacecraft problems: safe pointing control and safe station keeping.
arxiv-2604-03636: Chen, Huang, and Cheng present FlueBricks, a kit for learning sound science by building flute-like instruments from blow, echo, and link modules that carry air-sound traits. Joining modules shows how the blowhole, tube length, and tone-hole placement change onset, pitch, and timbre through hands-on play. A small study with 12 people, from beginners to pro players, finds users flipping between designer and player roles. They base designs on known instruments and reuse modules beyond their planned jobs.
arxiv-2604-03836: João Luzio and colleagues cut the cost of semantic visual search with a multi-scale artificial fovea. Their SemBA attention system reads meaning from scenes with deep detectors, but full-resolution input is slow. The new module keeps full sharpness at the center and blurs outer rings by downsampling, mimicking peripheral vision. Tests on target-present search showed lower processing cost, better scanpath prediction, and near-human consistency.
arxiv-2604-03936: Sam Rosen, Eric Chi, and Jason Xu offered a biconvex tweak to convex biclustering for high-dimensional data. Rather than dropping noisy traits outright, their method learns and weighs useful traits while finding biclusters. A fast method based on proximal alternating minimization comes with tuning guidance and quick sub-task solvers. Theory gives finite-sample bounds under sub-Gaussian errors, and tests plus a lymphoma microarray study showed strong finds.
arxiv-2604-04136: Ao Li and team proposed a new exposure-correction approach built for photos where exposure errors vary across regions. A Spatial Signal Encoder predicts adaptive modulation weights that guide several look-up tables for image transformation, with an HSL-based module for better color fidelity. Standard methods instead rely on global signals and shared-scale losses that miss local correction needs. An uncertainty-inspired non-uniform loss steers optimization focus by local restoration uncertainty, and tests showed superior qualitative and quantitative performance over state-of-the-art methods.
arxiv-2604-04636: Zu and three colleagues introduce Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks as an interpretable framework for crystal energy landscapes. Unlike standard neural networks with fixed activation functions, KANs use learned functions that reveal physical links. The team builds the Element-Weighted KAN, a composition-only model with top accuracy for formation energy, band gap and work function. Without explicit physical constraints, KANs uncover chemical trends aligned with the periodic table and quantum rules. The results show KANs offer high performance with scientific clarity, opening a new path for open, chemistry-based materials studies.
arxiv-2604-04736: Özdemir and five colleagues tackle the high cost of Bayesian learning, where drawing and testing many parameter samples strains memory and compute. Their fix, sampling parallelism, spreads sample tests across many graphics cards, cutting memory load and train time with no change to the model design. Tests show near-perfect scaling when sample count grows with the hardware. A mix with data parallelism helps, since each card can use its own random tweaks to the same batch and so need fewer training rounds.
arxiv-2604-04836: Sen sets out a new setup for spotting gravitational waves with charged resonant detectors known as Weber bars. The wave drives an optical setup, in a cavity setting where the bar sits inside a shielded cavity. When a wave strikes the bar, the bar emits a photon, and that emission marks the detection. The tuned spontaneous emission setup, he argues, could point toward a more efficient next generation of gravitational wave detectors.
arxiv-2604-04936: Allu and three colleagues improve how web pages are split for retrieval-augmented generation, where fixed, rule-based, or fully agentic splitting wastes tokens and scales poorly. Their Web Retrieval-Aware Chunking framework separates text extraction from semantic chunk planning, representing parsed pages as structured, ID-addressable units. Language models then decide only how to group units for retrieval, rather than generating text. That restraint cuts token use, removes a hallucination path, and is easier to debug for large-scale web ingestion.
arxiv-2604-05336: Kang, Suresh, Saad-Falcon, and Mirhoseini build TRACE, a training loop that turns an AI agent's own failures into lessons instead of fine-tuning blindly on target tasks. It contrasts successful and failed runs to name the missing skills, then builds a small training world for each skill that rewards using it. Compact adapters trained per skill are blended into one model. Gains run to about 15 points on a customer-service benchmark and a software-engineering benchmark alike, beating strong rivals while using under a fourth of their training runs.
arxiv-2604-05636: Bou and nine colleagues test whether ordinary broadcast soccer videos can reveal player fatigue without wearables or lab tests. From game-state reconstruction they derive speed and acceleration tracks and build acceleration-speed profiles across clips and a full half. Broadcast footage recovers fatigue-compatible patterns, though noise, calibration error, and cuts limit precision.
arxiv-2604-05736: Ruffenach and Chevillard stretch Gaussian multiplicative chaos models of turbulent dissipation from space alone to space and time. Recalling Mandelbrot and Kahane's cascade roots, they widen the even dissipation model to a space-time frame. Direct number runs of Navier-Stokes flow test the known spatial facts and the new time claims.
arxiv-2604-05936: Černák re-checks Slovakia's mass antigen testing at national scale, pushing back on claims that drives cut spread. Fine-grained re-checks show timing gaps in spread rates, cases, and deaths, with death-to-admission ratios moving the wrong way as rules bit. He claims testing kept people moving more than in the United Kingdom, with drives followed by more deaths and stressed health care.
arxiv-2604-06036: Zou and colleagues present CodecSight, a system serving vision-language models over video streams that reuses codec metadata to guide both visual encoding and language-model prefilling. Codec change signals prune patches before encoding, cutting visual work and tokens, while codec frame types steer selective key-value refresh across windows. Across three models and four workloads, the system serves up to 3.3 times as many concurrent streams and shortens time to first token, cutting executed FLOPs by up to 93 percent with quality down under five percentage points.
arxiv-2604-06136: Eremenko, Kulikov, and Sodin settle when a meromorphic function that omits three values must have bounded type. For a function defined on a curved half-plane set by an even, positive, nonincreasing function m, omitting three distinct values forces bounded type in the upper half-plane. That holds exactly when the logarithmic integral of m converges. When that integral diverges, the authors construct a counterexample: a function omitting three values yet of unbounded type. The result settles a century-old question going back to Rolf Nevanlinna.
arxiv-2604-06236: Lee argues that language models have made publishing failure newly urgent. Scientific publishing filters out negative results, and models inherit that positive bias while facing a shortage of high-quality training data and serving as research tools and peer reviewers. The paper analyzes three ways models change the value of failure data, showing its absence degrades their utility as tools, data consumers, and reviewers alike. It outlines experimental protocols to validate these claims and discusses the conditions that could let a failure-inclusive culture emerge.
arxiv-2604-06436: Bhatt and eight colleagues prove no continuous, utility-preserving input-cleaning wrapper defense can make every language-model output strictly safe. With connected prompt spaces, every defense fails somewhere, and the paper pins down where. Boundary fixation leaves threshold-level inputs unchanged; Lipschitz regularity leaves a band around fixed boundary points near-threshold; transversality leaves a positive-measure set strictly unsafe. The three cannot coexist. Discrete parallels need no topology. Other routes, like training-time alignment, stay open; Lean 4 verifies the theory, tested on three models.
arxiv-2604-06536: Hashmi and two colleagues build a multi-region arbitrage model for a battery linking two markets. Most models cover single markets only, leaving cross-border value unclear. Their formulation covers capacity, ramping, losses, and market prices. Disjunctive linearization gives a mixed-integer program. It forces simultaneous charging or discharging across markets. Belgian-UK prices over eight years show multi-region participation lifts revenue over 40 percent above local operation, while congestion cuts gains. Cross-border access improves profitability, and pseudo-efficiency boosts utilization, dropping less profitable cycles.
arxiv-2604-07036: Piatrashyn and nine colleagues address the cost tradeoff with ReDAct. Agents inherit language models' hallucinations, and in settings one mistake can ruin the trajectory. Larger models hallucinate less but cost more. ReDAct pairs a small cheap model with a large expensive model. Decisions defer to the large model when uncertainty passes a calibrated threshold. In ALFWorld and MiniGrid, deferring about 15 percent of decisions matches large-model quality while cutting costs.
arxiv-2604-07236: Jung and Son measure how much of a planning agent's skill lives in its harness rather than its language model. They split a harness for noisy Collaborative Battleship into four layers, from belief tracking through declarative planning and symbolic reflection to a language-model revision gate. Across 54 games, declarative planning does the heavy lifting, adding 24.1 percentage points of win rate with no language-model calls. Symbolic reflection shows real but cancelling effects, while language-model revision fires on only 4.3 percent of turns.
arxiv-2604-07336: Oehl and Tröster build a non-Gaussian likelihood for weak-lensing two-point correlations, where Gaussian approximations strain most on large scales. Their copula approach combines exact one-dimensional marginals with a dependence structure taken from the exact multivariate likelihood, allowing efficient evaluation. The copula form matches simulated sampling distributions better than Gaussian ones, especially on large scales. It can shift the S8 parameter by about one standard deviation for thousand-square-degree surveys, but barely moves it for ten-thousand-square-degree areas.
arxiv-2604-07536: Ye and three colleagues present TrustDesc, a system blocking tool poisoning in language-model apps by generating descriptions from code. Attackers poison tool descriptions with hidden malicious orders or false claims to steer model behavior and tool choice, and old guards fail against hidden poisoning. TrustDesc uses a three-step chain: SliceMin extracts minimal tool-relevant code slices, DescGen writes descriptions while curbing hostile bits, and DynVer refines them through checks. On 52 tools, TrustDesc yields true descriptions, improves task success, and curbs hidden poisoning at root with low cost.
arxiv-2604-07836: Yu and seven colleagues present LCMP, a distributed routing framework for remote direct memory access traffic between data centers. Multiple paths between data centers show lopsided quality, delayed congestion signals, and collisions when flows choose at once, defeating older routing methods. LCMP scores path quality centrally and reads compact congestion signals on switches for fast reaction. It filters out high-cost options and hashes within the survivors to preserve variety. An eight-site testbed tests low cost, low latency, and crowding response.
arxiv-2604-08336: Yanowsky and Weinshall address forgetting in continual learning, where a model trained on new tasks loses old skills. When the replay store is tiny, they argue, which past examples get kept matters most. Their MERS method picks stored examples with a graph that blends label based features with self taught features, which capture class meaning without labels. On CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet it beat single feature rivals, most clearly when memory was scarce, without adding weights or replayed volume.
arxiv-2604-08436: Nath introduces deck transformations for developable complexes of groups, borrowing the covering space idea from topology. He builds the universal development from path classes, grouping paths that count as the same, rather than using the usual build. That path based setup then gives a natural account of the deck transformation group.
arxiv-2604-08736: Aoki, Kikukawa, and Takemoto establish the exact SL(2,Z) structure of lattice Maxwell theory with a theta term in the modified Villain formulation. Although the ultra local action becomes non ultra local under Poisson resummation, a non local transformation built into the S-transformation removes that non locality. The result is exact SL(2,Z) duality. Wilson and 't Hooft loops then transform properly up to a phase from nontrivial self linking, and the resulting structure closely resembles non spin Maxwell theory.
arxiv-2604-08836: Jain and four colleagues present CatalogStitch, model free methods for catalog image making that remove tedious manual fixes. A size aware mask math adapts the target region to products of varied sizes from just a product image and background. A blocking aware hybrid repair method preserves blocking parts pixel exactly. A 58 example benchmark covers aspect ratio mismatch and blocking heavy cases, and tests with three leading blending models show steady gains across diverse catalog cases.
arxiv-2604-08936: Liu and five colleagues propose M-IDoL, a medical foundation model trained without labels that splits what it learns by imaging type instead of blending every modality into one embedding. Blending, they argue, blurs modality identity and variety, weakening later clinical tasks. Pretrained on 1.15 million medical images, the model tops 20 rival foundation models across 21 downstream tasks spanning five modalities, from X-ray and fundus to pathology. Its learned features separate imaging types cleanly while picking out fine detail within each.
arxiv-2604-09536: Logan and McKinnon prove that elliptic curves sitting on certain modular curves must suffer bad reduction at a specified prime. The prime's behavior splits the proofs into quite different arguments. As one instance, every elliptic curve with cyclic torsion of order 20 over either specified quadratic field has bad reduction at all primes over 3. The prime splits in the first field and stays inert in the second, forcing separate lines of attack.
arxiv-2604-09836: Waters and 22 co-authors present COMPOSITE-Stem, a benchmark holding 70 expert-written tasks across math, physics, biology, and chemistry, curated by PhD experts. The benchmark mixes exact-match grading and rule-based rubrics with a language-model-as-jury grading method, for flexible grading of science-rich outputs. Using a mixed Terminus-2 agent harness within the Harbor test suite, the team tests four frontier models. The top model hits 21 percent, showing the benchmark captures skills beyond current agent reach.
arxiv-2604-09936: Larraín-Hubach, Shapiro, and Vodev prove solver bounds for magnet Schrödinger engines, growing earlier results to larger classes of charge and magnet fields decaying faster than any power. The bounds cover slopes of the weighted solver, uniform in spectral knob and order. The bounds also hold for the Dirichlet self-adjoint form outside a non-trapping obstacle, if the magnet field dies there. As a use, the wave local energy decay rate is found: for stretched-exp fields, the rate is stretched-exp in time.
arxiv-2604-10036: Palmer, Cihak, Avitabile, and Kilpatrick add astrocyte support to neural field models of working memory. Sustained activity there depends on synapses that deplete and recover a shared resource pool. Their model lets astrocytes recycle and spread that resource by diffusion. The paper derives steady bump profiles with conditions for width and amplitude on a ring network. Analysis and simulations show a two-stage stabilizing effect. Diffusion smooths resource imbalances from small shifts, and replenishment feeds that smoothing back to synapses, suppressing drift.
arxiv-2604-10136: Blasone, De Siena, Lambiase, Micciola, and Simonov track entanglement in helicity degrees of freedom in QED scattering. At fixed momentum, scattering acts as a broad measurement, leaving a measured state. The team models these processes with quantum maps whose spectra set entanglement changes. For fermion-only scattering, full starting entanglement is always preserved. Iterating the maps on any starting states yields fixed points that are mostly asymptotic pure fully entangled states. The same maps explain processes mixing fermions and photons. Their key traits trace to QED's discrete symmetry.
arxiv-2604-10536: Luo, Wen, and Guo map heat flow in a momentum keeping fluid from flat to full space. Computer runs track a mesoscopic fluid built from multi particle collisions. Three regimes show up: size growing ballistic flow, size free kinetic flow, and fluid like flow. Flat systems grow logarithmically in the fluid regime, while full space systems settle finite. The crossover from odd two dimensional transport to plain Fourier flow now rests on firm numbers.
arxiv-2604-10736: Raj and Conway present BlasBench, an open benchmark for Irish speech recognition that fixes a gap in multilingual testing: current benchmarks apply no Irish-aware text normalization. The harness includes a standalone normalizer preserving fadas, lenition, and eclipsis, plus reproducible scoring and per-utterance predictions. Benchmarking 12 systems across four architecture families on Common Voice and FLEURS Irish data, they find all Whisper variants exceed 100 percent word error rate through insertion-driven hallucination. Microsoft Azure leads at 22.2 percent on Common Voice, while the best open model reaches 30.65 percent.
arxiv-2604-11036: Vinod and Erk present an uncertainty-aware, web-conditioned pipeline for science fact-checking in biomedicine and materials science. Existing systems often hallucinate or reason poorly on technical, compositional claims checked against an evidence snippet. Their pipeline splits claims into atomic predicate facts, aligns them to snippets via vectors, and checks them with an evidence-grounded checker. Only facts with uncertain support trigger restricted web search over trusted sources. When found evidence conflicts with the given context, the system abstains with a not-enough-information label rather than dropping context.
arxiv-2604-11236: Gommes derives exact formulas for the surface correlation functions of dead-leaves models, where space is filled in sequence by random overlapping grains, like leaves falling on the ground. The expressions hold for any grain shape and any dimension. Examples include identical spherical grains and a dead-leaves version of a Debye random medium, whose surface-surface correlations nearly match numerical reconstructions while its pore-surface correlations differ distinctly. A general Boolean-model formula falls out as a byproduct.
arxiv-2604-11736: Sharapov and Shcherbatov study Maxwell-Chern-Simons on 3D noncommutative spacetime with a fixed spacelike Poisson structure. Using symmetry, they build exact answers for pointlike electric and magnetic charges. Noncommutativity acts as a regulator, giving finite total energy and fixing the self-energy blow-up. Some depend non-perturbatively on the noncommutativity setting and allow any magnetic flux. They also present a noncommutative Gauss's law, which frames them.
arxiv-2604-11936: Khanure, Gour, Li, and Jue tackle network slice embedding over space-division multiplexed elastic optical networks. There, slices need coordinated spectrum and compute resources under shifting traffic. Earlier studies of routing, modulation, core, spectrum, and compute usually treat those dimensions apart. Their Waypoint Assisted Multi Segment Slice Mapping scheme couples compute placement with spectrum allocation in sequence. It improves acceptance ratios by up to 27 percent under high load and cuts total provisioning cost by up to 47 percent against the baseline.
arxiv-2604-12236: Muhammad and Liu improve multi-axis digital light processing for printing curved automotive parts without wasteful supports. Tilting a robotic arm to cure resin at varied angles creates non-uniform layer thickness, which old systems handle by splitting layers and adding time and supports. Their variable exposure method instead divides layers into sublayers and tunes ultraviolet duration to local thickness via a cure-depth equation, cutting layer counts, print time, and supports.
arxiv-2604-12336: Wu and three colleagues present GeM-EA, an evolutionary algorithm for streaming data-driven optimization where data arrive continuously and concept drift shifts the landscape. Upon detecting drift, a bi-level meta-learning strategy quickly sets up the surrogate from environment-relevant priors, while a linear residual term tracks global trends. A multi-island strategy reuses past knowledge through generative replay. Tests on benchmark problems show faster adaptation and stronger robustness than leading methods.
arxiv-2604-12536: Kyra Delray and four colleagues release MCAnalysis, a package for studying menstrual cycle effects in digital health data. Standard open tools for quantifying cyclic effects have been lacking. The package processes period dates and labels cycle days from menstruation onset. It filters implausible cycles, normalizes outcomes per person, and fits cyclic models. Bootstrap intervals and turning points yield phase-specific trend estimates. A demo on 2,816 app users covers 15 wearable and self-reported outcomes. Nine of 15 outcomes show cycle links across sleep, mood, symptoms, and activity.
arxiv-2604-12836: G. Russano and 15 colleagues watch a coronal mass ejection and its wave trains. Metis on Solar Orbiter imaged the October 8-9, 2022 eruption at 0.3 astronomical units. Running difference images sharpen the front, and height-time plots track speeds. A 3D flux rope model plus other spacecraft views follow it to about five solar radii. Fast circular wavefronts at 500 kilometers per second with a three minute period appear on the flank. The team weighs quasi-periodic fast modes among other readings.
arxiv-2604-12936: Mina Ghodsi Yengejeh and seven colleagues revisit the angular size-redshift test with radio galaxies. VLBI sizes of jetted active galaxies probe size versus redshift. An expanded set, ten times larger than past studies, updates a 25-year-old test. Randomized catalogs give posteriors that never overlap real ones. Source size evolution trades off against matter density in a flat universe. Mock catalogs show matter density is measurable when scatter stays below about 20 percent. Thousands to 100,000 sources plus calibration and sharper selection could unlock its full power.
arxiv-2604-13836: Neuman and Tuschmann study potential games on bounded-degree unimodular random graphs, where players interact. In plain terms, one score guides every player. The measure defines a potential for finite and infinite games. Mass transport identifies the potential's first change with a root player's first-order rule. Under convexity, minimizers match quenched Nash equilibria, and vice versa. The thermodynamic limit holds along weakly convergent sequences. Examples give semi-explicit equilibria: linear-quadratic games via the random walk Green kernel, convex cases via Poisson equations. Every player faces the same score.
arxiv-2604-13936: Ritz-Zwilling and Dmytruk couple a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain to one cavity light mode. In the far-detuned fast-drive limit they work out a model where the cavity links fermions. Three many-body markers, checked by exact runs, show the cavity reshapes topology. Chiral symmetry stays intact in the ground state.
arxiv-2604-14136: Krahm and thirteen colleagues map molecular gas in the edge-on galaxy NGC 4565 with sharp ALMA carbon monoxide images reaching past 17 kiloparsecs. They find a central gap more like M31 than the Milky Way, plus a steady isotope ratio near 0.086 between 5 and 13 kiloparsecs. The molecular disk stays thin, about 79 parsecs tall, with little flaring. Clouds match those in similar galaxies, and a star-forming pileup on the ring dubbed the East Ring Pileup hosts a compact spot the team calls the Jewel.
arxiv-2604-14236: The CMS Collaboration hunts a four-lepton resonance above 250 GeV that decays through two intermediate bosons in 13 TeV proton-proton collisions. The study uses CMS data equal to 138 inverse femtobarns. New techniques boost sensitivity to a collimated dilepton pair reconstructed as a single merged object from a light boson decay. No significant excess over background predictions appears. The team sets upper limits on the production cross section, including previously unexplored phase space with dilepton masses from 0.4 to 15 GeV.
arxiv-2604-14436: Bazeia and Lehum build a rigid superspace setup for impurity changes in one space plus one time dimension, placing the impurity shape in a superfield. This spurion completion keeps supersymmetry visible in the action and shows which uneven backgrounds keep some supercharges. For static interface shapes, they fix the half-BPS condition and its projector, then derive a first-order BPS equation and an exact energy bound met by BPS solutions. Position-tied effects and derivative couplings can break that bound structure, motivating spurion extensions that keep control.
arxiv-2604-14836: Li, Kotz, Schwarzenberger, Koos, and Kippenberg report the first thin-film lithium tantalate devices on fused silica, not silicon. Lithium tantalate, used in wireless filters, offers lower DC drift, higher power handling, and lower birefringence than niobate. A slow-wave electrode matches microwave and optical velocities, yielding 64-gigahertz electro-optic bandwidth at a half-wave voltage of 1.53 volts, with headroom to 100 gigahertz if spectral biasing is removed. Bias drift stays constant down to 10 millihertz. One lane carried 440.6 gigabits per second with PAM8 signals, matching lithium niobate devices on quartz.
arxiv-2604-14936: Wang, Bodek, Ouellette, Shattuck, and O'Hern simulate granular beds under sub-critical flows with discrete element methods in 2D and 3D, varying friction and speeds. Sub-critical motion causes no bed compaction. Instead, bed strength in a direction tracks the fraction of surface grains a fluid force there can dislodge. Anisotropic strength lasts a time set by the Shields number. Static friction proves unnecessary for anisotropy, though friction changes its magnitude. The work advances understanding of bed erosion and stresses tracking surface fabric history, which couples to bed strength.
arxiv-2604-15036: Buonemani and colleagues study a short quantum-dot chain tuned to host simplified Majorana bound states, exotic quasiparticles prized for fault-tolerant computing. They place the chain inside a light cavity and work out how the light shifts the pairing that creates the states. Even with that shift, particle interactions can be screened so the tuned sweet spot survives. Attractive forces cancel when the cavity holds no photons, keeping the sweet spot within reach in a realistic setup.
arxiv-2604-15236: Pierucci and others argue AI safety must study agents in groups, not lone models or bare totals. As agents gain planning, memory, tools, identity, and long exchanges, group risks grow from talk, watching, and mutual sway. Single-agent and total-based methods miss the exchange patterns that create shared risk and the design levers that control them. Their manifesto defines agentic microphysics, the local setup where one agent's output becomes another's input, and generative safety, the method of growing risks from small-scale conditions to find tipping points.
arxiv-2604-15336: Feng and eight colleagues test whether feeding facial-expression cues into tutoring prompts makes language-model tutors more empathetic. A simulated student shows varied facial behavior while four tutor variants, from text-only to Action Unit methods, hold 960 multi-turn chats across three model backbones. Action Unit conditioning improves empathetic response on every backbone, with peak-frame selection beating random frames, at no cost to clarity.
arxiv-2604-15636: Zhang and Fang extend contract design with intermediate states revealed during delegation, beyond final outcomes alone. They compare pay-halfway contracts, which pay on intermediate as well as final states, against terminate-halfway contracts, which let the principal stop on bad intermediate states. Both can beat standard contracts, and the paper maps when and how much intermediate-state information helps.
arxiv-2604-15736: Xu and seven colleagues test video MLLMs as auto sports refs with RefereeBench, the first big ref test bed. It spans 11 sports, 925 checked videos, and 6,475 Q and A pairs, grading foul spotting, foul and penalty sorts, foul and penalty logic, entity spotting, and time pinning. Even top models land near 60 percent right, and the best open model, Qwen3-VL, hits just 47 percent. Models spot incidents and players well but fumble rule use and time pinning, and cry foul too oft on clean clips.
arxiv-2604-16136: Roy and Sarma study taming quantum measure noise in a magnon platform for force sensing. The setup joins a cavity with a movable mirror, a fixed mirror, a magnon mode, and an optical tuning amp. Magnon motion reshapes the added-noise spectrum, lifting sense. Meeting the coherent quantum noise cancellation criterion kills light-pressure back-action. A larger amp pump gain permits beyond-limit work at reduced laser power, easing power constraints. These gains offer a path to below-limit weak force sensing.
arxiv-2604-16436: Ghoreishee and colleagues improve spiking neural networks for self-driving cars, where turning dense camera input into sparse spikes loses information and weakens value estimates. Their fuzzy encoder-decoder uses trainable membership functions to build richer spike patterns, then a light decoder rebuilds continuous action values from spiking outputs. On the HighwayEnv benchmark, decision accuracy rose substantially and the gap to non-spiking multi-modal networks narrowed. The design suits fast, energy-lean driving systems that must decide in real time.
arxiv-2604-16536: Mazhar and Galhotra frame unlearning testing as a first-class software problem. As rules require cutting sensitive data from models, it offers a choice over full retraining. Tests need scope over proxy paths, checks finding leakage, cheap runs under query budgets, and black-box use. Their causal fuzzing makes capped probes to estimate leftover effects and produce leakage reports. Standard tracing checks can miss hidden influence from proxies, wipeout and subgroup masking.
arxiv-2604-16636: Lauritzen and Thomsen study when algebra endomorphisms lift to first-order flat lifts. A first-order flat lift of an algebra and an endomorphism gives a canonical Hochschild cohomology class with twisted bimodule coefficients. That class is zero exactly when the endomorphism admits a multiplicative lift. For an Azumaya algebra of fixed rank over a formally smooth center, an endomorphism lifts exactly when the induced center endomorphism preserves the Poisson structure from the algebra lift.
arxiv-2604-16736: Agyemang and colleagues explain output stalling, where agents quietly return empty replies for large files. They define Output Generation Capacity, the output given context state, smaller than the raw window. A split theorem proves delayed drawing is at least as token-cheap as direct writing when format extra exceeds one. Tuned choice maps output cost against available room into direct, chunked or delayed generation. Across three models and four document types, delayed drawing cuts output tokens by 48 to 72 percent and ends stalling. The tool ships as GEN-PILOT.
arxiv-2604-16836: Hasan, Ahmed and Roy propose a semantic segmentation framework in the hyperbolic Lorentz model. Curved space models hierarchical structure tightly with built-in uncertainty measure, unlike the shaky P-ball model. Text codes with meaning and visual cues guide layered pixel-level representations in Lorentz space. Optimization stays stable and fast without a curved-space tuner, and the tool fits with old flat architectures. Beyond cutting, the way gives free doubt guess, trust maps, edge drawing, recall and zero-shot results.
arxiv-2604-17036: Srivastava and three colleagues review evolution as navigation over fitness landscapes, maps linking genotypes, phenotypes, and fitness. The field's fast-growing work uses shared terms loosely, so they define key concepts and settle their own word choices. They survey links among epistasis, ruggedness, accessibility, and navigability, examine how neutral networks shape change, and propose a new outcome-based measure of navigability plus open questions.
arxiv-2604-17136: Mendonça studies the joined Fibonacci constant, formed by writing Fibonacci numbers one after another past the decimal point. He asks whether its digits are evenly spread, the property called normality. Classical rules for normality by concatenation fail for them because of their exponential growth. Numerical experiments on the first 500,000 of them in bases 10 and 2 suggest digit counts and block statistics behave like independent random fluctuations, pointing to deep digits as the remaining obstacle.
arxiv-2604-17236: Chakraborty and Nguyen build a model for data spread near a mix of flat, low-dimensional subspaces, each blurred by noise. They show the smallest such mix can be pinned down uniquely under broad conditions. They also work out how fast Bayes-style estimates close in on the truth when each part sits on a convex polytope. Simulations back the theory, which fits tasks like spectral unmixing and topic models, where hidden flat structure must be pulled from messy data.
arxiv-2604-17336: Lunde and eleven colleagues study how replacing cobalt with nickel changes the cold-temperature behavior of NdCo2, a cubic Laves compound prized for magnetic cooling. Cooling drives the pure material through structural transitions at 100 K and 42 K. Both transitions slide to lower temperatures as nickel rises, and the lower-temperature phase vanishes at higher nickel levels. Magnetic cooling power also falls, from over six degrees to under five degrees at the same field, as the magnetic moment shrinks.
arxiv-2604-17436: Aadi, Singla, and Dube refine lunar elevation models with shape-from-shading, using Orbiter High Resolution Camera images from Chandrayaan-2. Applying shading analysis to an independent image of the same region yields new topographic detail beyond what stereo pairs alone can give. Tests at three sites, including the lunar south pole, Cyrillus crater, and the Vikram landing region, show clearer slopes and fine crater shapes. A limiting case is also mapped, where wide pitch-angle separation and partial image coverage weaken the enhancement.
arxiv-2604-17536: Dastider and three colleagues model how two sulfur-bearing molecules found in the cloud TMC-1 stick to icy dust grains. Thioformyl cyanide and propynethial matter for the interstellar sulfur budget, yet how they lodge in grain mantles is poorly pinned down. Using water clusters of 6 to 16 molecules to stand in for amorphous solid water, the team finds a patchy binding landscape with desorption energies from 1500 to 4900 kelvin. Strongly bound cavity sites shift carbon-sulfur stretching modes, while deeply bound cyanide cavities boost light absorption strength.
arxiv-2604-17736: Qin and five colleagues introduce IncreFA, framing credit as ordered stepwise learning, so the system keeps learning as new models emerge. Image credit is a moving target as new generators appear monthly, making watermark, sorter, and reverse methods dead. The core problem is not spotting but the failure to adapt credit itself. IncreFA uses layered links among generative designs. It joins two parts. Hierarchical Constraints encode design layers through tuned split priors, splitting family-level constants from model-specific quirks. A Latent Memory Bank replays compact codes.
arxiv-2604-18136: Barba-González, Albertus, and Pérez-García compute the equation of state for the warm outer crust of a neutron star. The equation of state links pressure, density, and temperature. They run microscopic molecular-dynamics simulations, modeling ions as finite-size Gaussian charge clouds with electron screening. Results are tabulated with a neural-network parametrization added, and ion heat effects matter most at higher densities near the inner crust.
arxiv-2604-18536: Agdestein and Sanderse present IncompressibleNavierStokes.jl, a Julia package solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes system on offset square grids. The package offers matrix-free, hardware-neutral kernels built from one source for CPU or GPU runs, plus hand-written adjoint kernels for fast auto gradients. This gradient access lets neural closure models be trained after the fact inside a large-eddy run. Memory tuning permits exact direct runs at grids up to 840 cubed on a single GPU, and choppy channel flow results check out against known data.
arxiv-2604-18736: Frohn and nine colleagues describe a new in situ stencil method for making charge islands in topological insulators made superconducting by proximity. Ribbons of bismuth-antimony telluride are grown in place, then barriers, superconducting aluminum, and thin oxide layers are laid down at set angles, with no later steps. At low temperatures, the devices show strong Coulomb blockade and a sharp drop in low-energy current that goes away in a magnetic field. The method gives a flexible way to build new hybrid quantum devices from topological solids.
arxiv-2604-18836: Rappaport and ten colleagues report the first octupole pulsation mode in a delta Scuti star, found in the binary system TIC 287869463. From TESS data for some 50,000 candidate eclipsing binaries found by machine learning, they searched for multiplets split by multiples of the orbital frequency. The new mode combines two spherical harmonics, perturbed by tidal, Coriolis, and centrifugal forces into a new mode that is stationary on the star. Its two parts stay split by exactly six times the orbital frequency, and rise over time.
arxiv-2604-18936: Woodward and five colleagues compare reinforcement learning and supervised fine tuning for small reasoning models in quantum field theory. Verifiable training data is scarce, so they built a pipeline that creates synthetic problems and adapts human authored ones. They generated over 2,500 synthetic problems plus curated human adapted problems from arXiv and textbooks. Both methods beat the base model on every set, but supervised gains cluster on synthetic tasks while reinforcement learning generalizes better. Reinforcement learning tops supervised results on human sets and TPBench.
arxiv-2604-19036: Billington presents plausible reasoning: conclusions from facts and defeasible claims without numbers. He suggests seventeen principles and gives examples. Fourteen are necessary and three desirable, one not formally stated. He defines Plausible Logic, a first-order logic meeting all but two desirable principles and reasoning right on all examples. As far as he is aware, it is the only such logic. Plausible Logic has eight algorithms, since varied conclusions can follow. It condenses his book of the same title, whose proofs are omitted.
arxiv-2604-19136: Varghese, Anguluri, and Pal propose a joint plan for line parameter estimation and transformer calibration. This solves a tangle: phasor unit data ease calibration by removing extra hardware and outages, but line parameter estimation from such data needs calibrated transformers. It uses power system knowledge as constraints to estimate line values and calibrate transformers all at once. They test it on simulated and real phasor unit data and on a power system application using both data and line parameters.
arxiv-2604-19336: Sahu, Jawanpuria, and Sharma extend online federated learning, where clients learn from live data streams without sharing private data, by adding a stochastically extended adversary. In the standard setup, the adversary model rules out any benefit from parallel work and misses sources of spread in these problems. Under their framework, the loss stays fixed across clients, while the adversary picks each client's data mix on its own at each step. Their method pairs random gradient descent at clients with regular server pooling, and they prove bounds on network results.
arxiv-2604-19436: Wang introduces a new update rule for evolutionary strategy dynamics based on each person's decision information, mixing personal and social inputs. Past work on such systems has focused mainly on structural differences between people, not on how update rules differ. The new rule lets each person vary the weight of personal input and the amount of social input used. Cooperation rises markedly when highly connected people lean more on social input.
arxiv-2604-19536: Wang and colleagues present LiveVLN, a training-free framework for continuous vision-language navigation. Recent systems score strongly on benchmarks, yet real deployment remains stop-and-go. The sense-inference-execution loop blocks: after each observation, the controller waits for sensing, transmission, and model work before motion continues. Cutting action-generation cost alone does not remove that waiting. LiveVLN adds multi-step action continuation to pretrained navigators, overlapping motion with processing of new views. The result is smoother motion in real rooms.
arxiv-2604-19636: Luo and colleagues present CoInteract, a framework for physically consistent human-object interaction video synthesis. Such videos have broad real value in e-commerce, digital ads, and virtual sales. Current diffusion models, despite photorealistic rendering, still fail on structural stability of hands and faces, and on plausible contact. It takes a person image, a product image, text prompts, and speech audio, embedding two complementary designs into a Transformer backbone.
arxiv-2604-19936: Rahmani, Jafari Siavoshani, and Rohban revisit the debate over membership inference attacks, which try to tell whether a given sample trained a model. They test whether better generalization, via augmentation and early stopping, lowers attack success. Advanced generalization methods cut attack performance sharply, at times by up to one hundred times. Combining methods also helps, by adding randomness during training, and a study of over one thousand models confirms that generalization directly shapes attack success.
arxiv-2604-20236: Lin, Mei, and Zhang tackle candidate graph thinning for the travelling salesman problem, where strong solvers like LKH search small pre-picked sets. The two best thinning rules clash on density versus recall: alpha-Nearest stays dense with steady recall, while POPMUSIC runs sparser but loses recall as size grows. Their union closes the recall gap near six times the node count, tagging each edge by its source. A light classifier then drops the weakest edges, keeping at least 99.69 percent of optimal tour edges while cutting density 37 to 47 percent.
arxiv-2604-20336: Xu and five colleagues propose a flow-matching frame for two humans sharing one object in joint handling. A generative model derives clear handling plans from the object's affordance and spatial layout, steering motion flow toward success. A rival interaction prior then fosters natural poses and true-to-life person-to-person play. A stability-led simulation refines shaky interaction states through sampling-based tuning and tunes vector field fits directly, beating human-object rivals on touch hit rate, overlap, and spread match.
arxiv-2604-20436: Lipsanen and five colleagues propose Shift-Up, a set of guardrails for software work driven by generative AI. Vibe coding speeds up early prototypes, they note, but often lets the design drift, weakens traceability, and hurts upkeep. Shift-Up recasts proven practices, like executable requirements, architecture models, and decision records, as machine-readable guardrails for agent-driven coding. Early tests on building a web app find the guardrails steady agent behavior, cut drift, and push human effort toward design and checks.
arxiv-2604-20536: Nel and Hale present a stable method for building Laguerre pseudospectral differentiation matrices, number grids for derivatives. Their approach recasts the off-diagonal entries and gets all values at once with a fast routine that also makes the grid points. For diagonal entries they use a direct formula to improve accuracy. The build avoids the precision loss of classical formulas when near-equal numbers subtract. Tests show stronger robustness and high accuracy for larger node counts than standard builds.
arxiv-2604-21136: Anaya-Sánchez and Sánchez-Salcedo study small, highly eccentric bodies orbiting inside a disc that hosts a dense ring. For bodies moving with the disc's rotation and crossing the ring, orbits round out and pile up at the ring radius, turning the ring into a migration trap. Tangent orbits keep grazing the ring and accrete fastest. Bodies moving against the rotation instead drift inward, their eccentricity growing without ever crossing the ring again.
arxiv-2604-21636: Harry Penketh and 12 colleagues present microwave single-pixel imaging for margin assessment in excised breast tumours. A photo-induced transparency change in a silicon modulator under the sample maps reflectivity of tissue phantoms with sub-wavelength resolution. It maps hydration across 10 by 10 cm at about 1 mm resolution. Gelatin tumour phantoms with water shifts mimicking malignant-margin contrast test discrimination. The method finds, locates, and sizes inadequate margins up to 2 mm. Numerical modelling shows resilience across patients, making it promising for real-time use in surgery.
arxiv-2604-21836: Hosseini and three colleagues measure how single stimuli drive convergence between neural networks. Using a Generalized Procrustes method, they score intra-modal agreement among vision models with different training goals. Stimuli that vision models agree on most also align far better with language models, by up to a factor of two in DINOv2 pairings. The effect holds across selection criteria and model pairings, suggesting stimulus-level agreement shapes cross-modal convergence.
arxiv-2604-22036: VanVoorst and eleven colleagues introduce EgoMAGIC, an egocentric medical activity dataset from DARPA's Perceptually-enabled Task Guidance program. The dataset comprises 3,355 videos of 50 medical tasks, with at least 50 labeled videos per task. The medical training data has been released with an action detection challenge focused on eight medical tasks. From this dataset, 40 YOLO models were trained using about 2 million labels to detect 124 medical objects. The paper presents baseline action detection results for the eight tasks across three models, with the best method achieving average mAP 0.526 across the eight tasks.
arxiv-2604-22136: He and Yu argue wiring model agents straight to execution is unsafe, since correctness, context awareness, and alignment cannot be assumed at run time. They introduce Sovereign Agentic Loops, where models emit intents with justifications. A control plane checks intents against state and policy before execution. It pairs a membrane hiding identity-sensitive state with a linked Evidence Chain for audit and replay. In OpenKedge, it blocks 93 percent of unsafe intents at the policy layer, rejects the rest via consistency checks, and adds 12.4 ms median latency.
arxiv-2604-22336: Nakano and Takai propose a quantum sensing scheme for wave-like dark matter and high-frequency gravitational waves. It uses ion crystals in a Penning trap, with squeezed spin-motion states to lift signal-to-noise ratio. That setup enables super-Heisenberg scaling with ion number over a broad parameter range. They assess sensitivity to axion-like particles and dark photons, plus high-frequency waves, accounting for spin decoherence and dephasing. Ion crystals thus offer a platform for probing unexplored space for light dark matter and high-frequency waves.
arxiv-2604-22436: Wu and three colleagues offer AgentSearchBench, a test for finding fitting AI agents in the wild. Agent skills are mixed and execution-dependent, so text alone judges them poorly. Past tests assume set functions, controlled pools or executable queries only. Built from nearly 10,000 real agents, it frames search as retrieval and ranking under executable queries and high-level descriptions, scored by execution. Tests show a gap between semantic similarity and actual performance, exposing limits of description-based methods. Lightweight behavioural signals, including execution-aware probing, improve ranking a lot.
arxiv-2604-22736: Achilleos proves that deciding whether a plan exists stays undecidable even under tight limits. Goals are stated in modal logic, the start is a single epistemic state, and actions have preconditions reaching only one level of modal depth, with no postconditions at all. The question asks whether some sequence of knowledge-changing actions can reach the goal. Until this paper, whether that restricted version was decidable or not had remained open.
arxiv-2604-22836: Miao and six colleagues describe a video object segmentation system built around Sa2VA for a challenge track on referring expressions in video. Sa2VA first proposes a coarse mask trajectory. Planner, partition, scout, and refinement agents then check, search, and improve it, with a critic scoring candidates and a controller repairing weak hypotheses. If the referred object is absent, the system outputs empty masks rather than inventing one.
arxiv-2604-22936: Chelli and Perera simulate site-based models of alcohol mixtures in two dimensions to study ideal mixing, local clustering, and miscibility. Pairs tested include methanol-ethanol and methanol-octanol, spanning near and distant alcohols. Short and long alcohols stay miscible in two dimensions, unlike the phase separation seen in three dimensions. Short-range structure is dominated by charge ordering of hydroxyl head groups, while long-range patterns point to domain-like concentration fluctuations. Together these findings show a close link between charged head groups and hydrophobic tails.
arxiv-2604-23036: He and seven colleagues tackle supervised fine-tuning for mixture-of-experts models with fragile router layers. Dense mixing and load-balancing mitigate collapse but add noisy gradients that hurt performance. Pruning tests show rare experts encode useful knowledge, though discarding them degrades performance despite super experts activating more often. Their auxiliary-loss-free framework combines bias-driven sparsification with always-active gated condenser experts, preserving long-tailed expert information and beating state-of-the-art baselines by more than 2.5 percent on average across math and commonsense benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-23136: Gautam and three colleagues watch 15 researchers think aloud while using AI tools for early-stage research tasks such as finding literature, synthesis, and shaping ideas. They find confident AI wording hides uncertainty, making it harder to spot outputs needing close scrutiny, while opaque retrieval hides provenance. Trust proves fragile and context-bound, easily eroded, yet researchers develop workarounds that restore scholarly judgment under uncertainty. The study frames AI-mediated research as a responsibility problem rooted in lived practice, urging deliberate integration that preserves accountability and trust.
arxiv-2604-23236: Ford and three colleagues use exhaustive symbolic regression to find better forms for galaxy luminosity, stellar mass, and halo mass functions. Standard fitting formulas were chosen by eye, so they score every function up to a set complexity by description length, weighing accuracy against complexity. Many discovered functions beat Schechter forms for luminosity and stellar mass, and Press-Schechter and Warren/Tinker forms for halo mass. Adding physicality checks on extrapolation and integration yields optimal low-complexity forms, plus a general frame for automating function discovery on other datasets.
arxiv-2604-23436: Wang, Du, and Na give streaming Newton methods a sound way to report uncertainty, a task that usually demands costly matrix updates. Their online Newton method averages Hessians and solves each step approximately with an accelerated sketch-and-project routine, matching first-order methods' cost. They prove convergence and asymptotic normality of the final iterate, build a fully online covariance estimator, and confirm the method on regression tests.
arxiv-2604-24336: Lombardi and five colleagues track 51,056 Finnish graduates for up to 25 years. Higher gene scores for education predict income growth, but only among the college group. 90th-percentile graduates earn EUR 45,392 more discounted lifetime income than 10th-percentile graduates. The effect is absent for high-school workers and does not show at labor market entry. Instead, job-to-job moves toward better firms drive the later gap. With parents' indices in 12,871 trios, the gap falls by 71 percent, with fathers' effects above the offspring's own.
arxiv-2604-24536: Bhattacharyya and eight colleagues test ways to draft fair compromises between people who disagree about a shared place, using language models as the drafters. They compare four prompting tricks on thousands of clashing views. Fifty readers then judge the best outputs. The winning trick feeds back how evenly a draft treats each side, beating plain step-by-step reasoning, and the judged drafts then train two smaller models that no longer need that scoring step.
arxiv-2604-24636: Oliveira documents a five-day, 204-commit effort to put small language models into Palabrita. Palabrita is a production Android word-guessing game, run fully on device. The design retreats from letting the model generate whole structured puzzles. Instead, curated word lists supply the words. The model writes only three short hints, falling back deterministically if it fails. He catalogs five failure types, from format and constraint violations to latency and model-selection instability. Defensive parsing, retry and prompt-hardening tactics tamed them.
arxiv-2604-24736: Ermakov builds a parametric theory of inference for moderate deviation probabilities. His proofs expand the log likelihood ratio in a Taylor series based on the Hellinger metric. He proves the Large Deviation Principle in this zone for Bayesian and maximum likelihood estimators. A uniform approximation of the log likelihood ratio and a theorem on posterior focus also hold in this zone. The zone sits between central-limit cases and large-deviation cases.
arxiv-2604-25136: Pustejovsky and Krishnaswamy propose Frictive Policy Optimization, a framework for language-model policies. It governs not just what a model says but when and how it steps in. Clarification, verification, challenge, redirection and refusal act as explicit controls. They shape belief, commitment and uncertainty over time. Choices follow expected downstream epistemic quality, not immediate reward alone. The paper adds a taxonomy of frictive moves, a functional for several failure modes and a way to test epistemic conduct.
arxiv-2604-25536: Liu and Cao build analytic tools for the Fourier modes of waves from highly eccentric binaries in post-Newtonian theory. Their methods handle the quasi-Keplerian description at large eccentricity. They also expand the enhancement function that enters the tail radiation. Those results feed an endpoint-constrained method that computes modes far faster at large eccentricity. Error stays within one thousandth, for modes up to 200 and eccentricities up to 0.9, where the approximation remains valid. The tools aid frequency-domain modeling of such binaries.
arxiv-2604-25736: Andreeva and seven colleagues examine how coupling between disks changes magnetoplasma waves in a square lattice of electron-system disks etched from a gallium arsenide quantum well. Using magneto-optical terahertz spectroscopy, they track the collective modes as the lattice period shrinks and coupling grows stronger. At large separations the system shows modes matching single-disk excitations. As disks draw closer, the magnetoplasma dispersion changes. The study maps how inter-disk coupling reshapes collective behavior in these lattices.
arxiv-2604-26036: André-Hoffmann and five colleagues introduce BADPIT, tracking ultraviolet brightenings before major solar flares. BADPIT detects brightenings across SDO/AIA channels with a 3-sigma intensity rule and a power-law divergence rule. It runs 24 hours on a flaring region, AR 11429, and a quiescent region, AR 13186. Both share a Hale class, yet the flaring region shows far more brightenings. Power-law events appear often only in the flaring region, absent in the quiet one. Both threshold methods can distinguish imminent flaring hours before major flares.
arxiv-2604-26136: Abebe and Moslem tackle cross-lingual voice cloning for scientific speech. The challenge is preserving a speaker's voice identity while generating speech in another language. Their submission to a 2026 spoken-language-translation shared task first benchmarks several leading cloning models. Tests cover scientific texts in Arabic, Chinese, and French. The authors then build systems on the OmniVoice foundation model. Data augmentation through multi-model ensemble distillation improves intelligibility and speaker similarity, with gains varying across languages.
arxiv-2604-26736: Perazzo and Capecchi bridge theory and deployment for FlyClient, a lightweight blockchain verification protocol enabling proof-of-work validation with minimal data for wallets, Internet-of-Things devices, and cross-chain bridges. Despite its promise, FlyClient remains experimental, with few real deployments and performance tests. The paper offers a new adversary model that parametrizes a verifier under a concrete economic reading while saving proof space. It also gives the first practical FlyClient prover for a production blockchain in Zcash. Two optimizations shrink proof size, the first needing no consensus change.
arxiv-2604-26836: Frauenknecht and four colleagues introduce UPSi, a safety filter that checks safety for reinforcement-learning exploration with probabilistic ensemble neural nets. Old filters leaned on first-principles models or Gaussian processes, limiting scale, while ensemble models lacked strict uncertainty checks. UPSi frames future outcomes as reachable sets and adds a clear certainty rule that blocks model exploitation. Tested in Dyna-style model-based learning on standard safe benchmarks, it lifts exploration safety well over past neural filters while matching standard performance.
arxiv-2604-27436: Klement and four colleagues present the BUT system for the CHiME-9 MCoRec challenge, turning mixed talk from audio and video into speaker groups. Their target-speaker model handles audio in one pass, feeding a pretrained Parakeet speech model cues from AV-HuBERT. To group speakers, they use a language model to estimate topic likeness, followed by clustering. On the development set, the system reaches 33.7 percent word error rate with a strong clustering F1 score, and it ranks second on the test set.
arxiv-2604-27736: Biskowski and three colleagues study the celestial three-gluon amplitude against a dilaton background through Stieberger-Taylor-Zhu Mellin-Liouville. The first map leaves a Liouville-Mellin gap, resolved via shape match and semi-classic Liouville fit. This fixes operator scaling and setting map, yielding a tidy link expansion. From the full DOZZ three-point function come leading and next terms. The leading term gives the tree-level Yang-Mills amplitude at small total motion, and the one-loop fix takes Bessel form.
arxiv-2604-27836: Sankar, Miliotis, and Caton extend HADOF tests, decomposing large QUBOs into smaller subproblems solved on quantum or classical hardware. They benchmark HADOF on IBM QPUs in sequential runs, single-QPU parallel runs, and multi-QPU parallel runs, toward High Performance Quantum computing. On IBM hardware, wall clock time falls 3 to 4 times with four QPUs versus sequential runs, with comparable solution quality. Even single QPU execution benefits from job orchestration, yielding up to 3 times speedup, and simulations predict over 5 times faster.
